blocks.text: Brentwood Park at a glance, September 2026

Brentwood Park is a Burnaby community around Brentwood Town Centre. In September 2026 it had 381 homes listed: 360 condos and townhomes and 21 houses. It ranks number 1 of 35 Burnaby communities by condo and townhome listings, and houses are 6% of what is for sale.

Brentwood Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

490 condos sold in Brentwood Park with a median price of $693,750 (the middle half sold between $577,625 and $813,750), taking a median of 27 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $884 per square foot, a median year built of 2020 and a median strata fee of $472 a month. 20 houses sold in Brentwood Park with a median price of $1,750,000 (the middle half sold between $1,644,989 and $1,958,500), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 97.2% of the last list price; 10% sold above list. They had a median $699 per square foot, a median year built of 1958 and a median lot of 6,710 square feet.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Brentwood Park
The Amazing Brentwood, Tower 1 — 4510 Halifax Way

A concrete high-rise by Shape Properties (the master-plan developer), built in 2019 per current listings, which describe floor-to-ceiling windows, concierge, a large gym with yoga/dance studio, outdoor recreation area, music room, meeting room and 2 guest suites. Unit count and published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked. A portal mapping of the development lists its three buildings as 4510 Halifax Way (Tower 1), 1955 Alpha Way (Tower 2) and 4650 Brentwood Boulevard (Tower 3).
The Amazing Brentwood, Tower 2 — 1955 Alpha Way
The development's second tower per the portal mapping above.
The Amazing Brentwood, Tower 3 — 4650 Brentwood Boulevard

Built in 2021 per current listings, by Shape Properties; listings describe a 1- and 2-bedroom tower with 9-foot ceilings and floor-to-ceiling windows above The Amazing Brentwood retail. One current listing records pets as "Cats OK" in its fields. Unit count and published rental/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Altus (SOLO District) — 4485 Skyline Drive

Built in 2017 per current listings, by Bosa / Appia ("SOLO District - Altus Tower by Bosa's Appia"); listings describe geothermal heating and A/C, 9-foot ceilings, 24-hour concierge, a gym, outdoor sports court, rooftop terrace and a 49th-floor sky lounge. Unit count and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Stratus (SOLO District) — 2008 Rosser Avenue

Current listings describe Stratus at Solo District by Bosa with geothermal A/C and heating, 24-hour concierge, fitness centre, sauna, steam room, party room, BBQ area, dog park and EV charging. Year built and unit count: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked. Published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Cirrus (SOLO District) — 2085 Skyline Court

Current listings describe Cirrus at Solo District with panoramic mountain and city views, steps to Whole Foods and Brentwood Town Centre Station. Year built, unit count and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED. A building-portal summary describes SOLO District as three buildings — 2008 Rosser Avenue (Stratus), 4485 Skyline Drive (Altus) and 2085 Skyline Court (Cirrus).
Triomphe — 1888 Gilmore Avenue

Built in 2020 per current listings, by Millennium; listings describe a concrete tower with central A/C, over 13,000 sq ft of amenities (outdoor pool, hot tub, sauna, steam room, fitness centre, BBQ terrace, 2 guest suites, concierge, EV charging), 1 parking and 1 storage locker per unit in the listings checked, one block from Gilmore SkyTrain. Note a naming trap in the feeds: at least one listing service labels units at this address "Gilmore Place," a different Onni project on the same avenue — verify the building name on the strata plan. Unit count and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Escala — 1768–1788 Gilmore Avenue
Built in 2019, 42 storeys, 520 units, per a furnished-rental building profile, with over 15,000 sq ft of amenities. Published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Two Gilmore Place (Gilmore Place) — 2108 Gilmore Avenue

Completed in 2024, 64 storeys, 643 apartments, developed by Onni Group, at Lougheed Highway and Gilmore Avenue immediately north of Gilmore Station; at 215.8 metres it is described as the tallest building in British Columbia. The Gilmore Place first phase is described by industry reporting as entirely for-sale market residential homes; the disclosure-statement / strata position for a specific unit is UNCONFIRMED until read. The wider Gilmore Place project address is also given as 2168 Gilmore Avenue & 4186 Lougheed Highway, with three towers in phase one.

Built in 2022, 50 storeys, developed by Concord Pacific and completed in 2022, per a building profile. The same profile series gives Hillside West Tower 1 at 4720 Lougheed Highway, built in 2023, and repeats a figure of 892 units for both towers individually — that unit count is internally inconsistent and is treated as UNCONFIRMED; do not quote it. Anola Place — 2041 Bellwood Avenue

A 50-storey residential high-rise of 407 condominiums by Concord Pacific, phase two of the Concord Brentwood master-planned community (26 acres, 13-acre park), slated for completion in early 2027 per a presale source. Brentwood Block — 2180 Alpha Avenue

Grosvenor has started construction on Phase 1 of Brentwood Block, a 7.9-acre pedestrian-focused master plan: a 41-storey residential strata tower, two rental towers, a new 100,000 sq ft Brentwood Community Centre and 180,000 sq ft of commercial, with 1,279 rental homes in Phase 1; the community centre's completion is anticipated for late 2029, and the full master plan is roughly 3,500 homes including 2,450 rental homes.
Streets, schools and getting around Brentwood Park

items.t: Brentwood Park is the residential sub-area in north-west Burnaby around Brentwood Park Elementary, south and east of the Brentwood Town Centre. "Brentwood Park" is the GVR board sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report under community "Burnaby," and it is also the name of Brentwood Park Elementary School (SD41); the City planning framework for the area is the Brentwood Town Centre, one of Burnaby's four town centres. A City page using "Brentwood Park" as an official neighbourhood name was not confirmed, and the City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area — exact MLS boundary streets: UNVERIFIED.

Where the condo stock concentrates: in two clusters. The tower cluster rings the town centre and its two Millennium Line stations — the Amazing Brentwood towers at Willingdon and Lougheed, the SOLO District towers on Rosser Avenue and Skyline Drive/Court, Concord Brentwood along the south side of Lougheed Highway, Gilmore Place and Triomphe / Escala at Gilmore Avenue, and Affinity on Douglas Road — while an older mid- and high-rise cluster (Vantage Point, Anola Place) sits on Bellwood Avenue above the residential streets, and low-rise product (Memento on Beta Avenue) fills in toward the houses.

SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: Burnaby-wide Condos & Townhomes median was $686,000, $763/sqft, 98% sale-to-list, 36 days on market in September 2026. There is no Brentwood Park sub-area median.
Main streets: Lougheed Highway runs along the town centre's south side, Willingdon Avenue runs south to Highway 1, Metrotown and BCIT, and Delta Avenue / Parker Street serve the residential grid.

Transit anchors: Brentwood Town Centre Station and Holdom Station, both Millennium Line, serve the area's edges; Brentwood Town Centre Station at Lougheed Highway and Willingdon Avenue is also an R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus connection point, and Gilmore Station (Millennium Line) serves the Gilmore Avenue towers at the sub-area's east side — Triomphe listings describe the building as one block / steps from Gilmore SkyTrain.

blocks.text: Good to know about Brentwood Park

items.t: The area research pass recorded Brentwood's tower names as UNVERIFIED because no building was confirmed on a developer or strata source in that pass.

BC's tallest building is in this sub-area. Two Gilmore Place, completed 2024 at the corner of Lougheed Highway and Gilmore Avenue, is 215.8 metres (708 ft) and 64 storeys — described as the tallest building in British Columbia — and its first phase sits immediately north of Gilmore Station.

A whole new block is under construction, and most of it is rental. Grosvenor's Brentwood Block Phase 1 pairs one 41-storey strata tower with two rental towers, 1,279 rental homes, a 100,000 sq ft City-owned Brentwood Community Centre (anticipated late 2029) and 180,000 sq ft of commercial — the full plan is roughly 3,500 homes, of which about 2,450 are rental. Future "Brentwood condo supply" headlines that count all 3,500 as condos overstate the strata share.

Concord Brentwood is a 26-acre, 10-tower plan, and its next phase is a 2027 presale. The master plan transforms 26 acres south of Lougheed Highway between Beta and Delta avenues into 10 residential towers around 13 acres of park; Oasis, its second phase at 4863 Dawson Street, is a 50-storey, 407-condo tower slated for completion in early 2027 — presale contracts there sit under REDMA until completion.

The same name, two tenures, two addresses. "Tower One" at The Amazing Brentwood is both a strata tower (4510 Halifax Way) in listing feeds and a purpose-built rental building (1820 Willingdon Avenue) on SHAPE's rental site. Any automated building count that merges them double-counts the sub-area's largest development.

The old stock is one street, not scattered. Vantage Point I and II and Anola Place all sit on Bellwood Avenue (2020, 2060 and 2041 Bellwood) — the sub-area's pre-town-centre high-rise pocket, with strata fees at Vantage Point I published as including heat and hot water, a cost structure the new towers do not share.

The zoning bylaw underneath every Brentwood rezoning changed on July 1, 2026. Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026) fully repealed and replaced the 1965 bylaw and moved many districts from FAR-based to height-based regulation — development copy written off the old bylaw's district names is stale, and the Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) now takes precedence over the older Brentwood community-plan maps.

items.t: "Brentwood Park" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby: the residential sub-area around Brentwood Park Elementary, south and east of Brentwood Town Centre, one of Burnaby's four town centres. Street-by-street boundaries for the MLS sub-area are UNVERIFIED — no City or board source read publishes them.
Transit anchors: Brentwood Town Centre Station and Holdom Station (Millennium Line) serve the sub-area, with the R2 Marine Dr / SFU rapid bus at Brentwood.

Schools: School District 41 (Burnaby) runs 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools with no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12), and catchments are address-based through the SD41 locator. Schools on the Province's list in and beside the sub-area include Brentwood Park Elementary (K–7), 1455 Delta Ave, Gilmore Community Elementary, 50 S Gilmore Ave, Kitchener Elementary, 1351 Gilmore Ave, and Burnaby North Secondary (8–12), 751 Hammarskjold Dr.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Brentwood Park

items.t: Form B diligence (the 1 strata complex above, and every tower strata documented in): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. The Springer Avenue complex's restrictions are UNCONFIRMED — the Form B and registered bylaws are the diligence, not listing copy.

SSMUH (R1): Burnaby's R1 district (consolidated June 2024) allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; minimum lot width 10 m, minimum lot area 281 m²; lots with two or more primary units may be stratified; permitted forms include single-family, duplexes, multiplexes, rowhouses and secondary suites. SSMUH speaks to the detached streets around the towers, not to the strata complexes themselves.

Presale protection (Oasis, Brentwood Block, Étoile Gold): under the Real Estate Development Marketing Act (REDMA), a presale buyer may rescind within 7 days after the later of signing the purchase agreement or receiving the disclosure statement (s. 21), and all deposits must promptly be placed in trust with a brokerage, lawyer, notary or prescribed trustee in a BC savings institution (s. 18).

blocks.text: Good to know about Brentwood Park

items.t: The sub-area's only standalone townhouse complex predates the entire tower district by four decades: the Springer Avenue strata was built in 1976, when Brentwood was a detached-house suburb; Two Gilmore Place, the 64-storey tower two blocks of streets away, completed in 2024.

Two complexes share the Springer Avenue name in listings — the 1976 strata at 2078–2082 Springer and the 2026 Slate tower at 2135 Springer. A search that does not separate them mixes a small wood-frame strata with a 45-storey concrete tower.
Burnaby's property-tax penalties cannot be waived by the City even for a one-day-late payment — the City states it has no authority to waive or modify them.

Burnaby rewrote its entire zoning bylaw effective July 1, 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815) and adopted a new OCP on December 9, 2025 — any Brentwood guide or listing sheet still citing the 1965 Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 or the 1998 OCP is out of date.

items.t: Nearby areas: Brentwood Town Centre to the north-west, Parkcrest and Lochdale to the east, Willingdon Heights and Capitol Hill to the north, and the Sperling–Duthie side to the south-east.

Roads and transit: Lougheed Highway runs along the town centre's south side, Willingdon Avenue runs south to Highway 1, Metrotown and BCIT, and Delta Avenue / Parker Street serve the residential grid. Brentwood Town Centre Station and Holdom Station, both Millennium Line, serve the area's edges; Brentwood Town Centre Station is also an R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus connection point. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Parks, library, health: Brentwood Park sits beside the elementary school the sub-area is named for, and the Jim Lorimer Park / Still Creek corridor is in the wider area; facility detail for Brentwood Park beyond that: UNVERIFIED. The Burnaby Public Library branch serving north Burnaby is the McGill Branch, 4595 Albert Street, north-east of the sub-area. The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health), in central Burnaby. No City recreation centre inside the sub-area was confirmed: UNVERIFIED.

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) operates 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide, with no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12. Schools in or beside this sub-area on the Province's list are Brentwood Park Elementary (K–7), 1455 Delta Ave, Gilmore Community Elementary (K–7), 50 S Gilmore Ave, and Kitchener Elementary (K–7), 1351 Gilmore Ave; the nearest secondary on the list is Burnaby North Secondary (8–12), 751 Hammarskjold Drive. School names are Ministry-listed names only.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Brentwood Park

items.t: Zoning — Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815): adopted Jun 9, 2026 and in effect Jul 1, 2026, replacing the former Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742), which is never cited as current for Burnaby. Burnaby consolidated its former single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District in June 2024.

OCP — Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan: adopted Dec 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 OCP; it takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict, and the Brentwood Town Centre framework sits within it. Community plans are adopted by Council as policy guidelines for rezoning and development applications.

Subdivision + servicing — Burnaby servicing-bylaw base number HELD UNCONFIRMED: the former servicing base number was renamed by Amendment Bylaw No. Confirm subdivision and servicing requirements with the City of Burnaby for the specific parcel.

Strata block (for completeness — no Brentwood Park bare-land strata is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Brentwood Park ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

Burnaby property taxes: City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date; Council approved a 2.9% property tax increase in the 2026–2030 Financial Plan, about $61 for the average home.

faq.q: Is Brentwood Park the same as the Brentwood Town Centre?
faq.a: No — Brentwood Park is the MLS® sub-area name for the residential streets around Brentwood Park Elementary, next to the Brentwood Town Centre; the town centre is the City's planning and shopping framework for the same north-west Burnaby area.

faq.q: What sold in Brentwood Park in September 2026?
faq.a: Condos & townhomes: 39 solds from 360 listings (11% sales ratio); detached: 3 solds from 21 listings (14%). Burnaby-wide, the median detached sale price was $1,825,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $686,000 that month (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which SkyTrain stations serve Brentwood Park?
faq.a: Brentwood Town Centre Station and Holdom Station, both on the Millennium Line, at the area's edges; Brentwood Town Centre Station also connects to the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus.

faq.q: Which elementary school is in Brentwood Park?
faq.a: Brentwood Park Elementary (K–7), 1455 Delta Ave, with Gilmore Community Elementary, 50 S Gilmore Ave, and Kitchener Elementary, 1351 Gilmore Ave, also in or beside the sub-area; confirm any address's catchment with the SD41 School Locator.

faq.q: When were Burnaby property taxes due in 2026?
faq.a: Friday, July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on outstanding current taxes after the July due date and a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

faq.q: How deep is the competition if I buy or sell a Brentwood condo?
faq.a: Burnaby-wide, the Condos & Townhomes median that month was $686,000 at $763/sqft, 98% sale-to-list, 36 days on market — community figures only; SnapStats publishes no Brentwood Park median.

Two Gilmore Place (2108 Gilmore Avenue) completed in 2024 at 64 storeys and 643 apartments — the tallest building in BC at 215.8 metres — and Concord Brentwood's Hillside East at 4890 Lougheed Highway is profiled as built in 2024, with Hillside West (4730 Lougheed) in 2022 and Amazing Brentwood Tower 3 (4650 Brentwood Boulevard) in 2021. Slate (2135 Springer Avenue) is marketed as Brentwood's newest landmark, but its completion year is UNCONFIRMED in the sources checked.

faq.q: Is the Amazing Brentwood tower at Willingdon a condo building?
faq.a: Careful — there are two near-identical names. The strata towers are at 4510 Halifax Way (Tower 1, 2019), 1955 Alpha Way (Tower 2) and 4650 Brentwood Boulevard (Tower 3, 2021). SHAPE's own rental site places "Tower ONE" purpose-built rental homes at 1820 Willingdon Avenue, professionally owned and managed by SHAPE — that building is rental, not strata. Confirm which address a listing belongs to before comparing.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Brentwood condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, whatever a directory or older bylaw says.

faq.q: What do strata fees cover in the older stock?
faq.a: It varies and is a Form B question. One concrete published example: a Vantage Point I (2020 Bellwood Avenue) listing states the strata fees include heat and hot water. The older Bellwood buildings also carry the elevator, parkade and envelope cycles their depreciation reports must now map every five years.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot in Brentwood Park?
faq.a: No verified one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering was verified in the research.

faq.q: How many homes can an R1 lot hold?
faq.a: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; minimum lot width 10 m and minimum lot area 281 m² for SSMUH lots, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified.
